newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Ikeda says will remain as foreign minister.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Ikeda says will remain as foreign minister.

text.p: Japan's Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda on Thursday withdrew an offer to resign from his post after consulting with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Jiji news agency reported.
"I will continue to deal with diplomatic issues to restore trust (in the Foreign Ministry)," Jiji quoted Ikeda as telling a news conference after his meeting with Hashimoto.
Earlier, Jiji and Kyodo news agencies said Ikeda offered to step down from his job to take responsibility for the Peru hostage crisis. The reports also said Hashimoto asked him to stay.

The four-month crisis ended on April 22 when Peruvian commandos raided the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and freed all but one of the 72 hostages. One hostage and two soldiers died while all 14 Marxist rebels were killed.
The Japanese news agency reports came soon before the Foreign Ministry was to announce a report on a government investigation into the affair.

The Japanese ambassador to Lima, Morihisa Aoki, was forced to give up his job last month after his return to Japan. Japanese media had accused Aoki, host of the party which was raided by the Marxist rebels last December, of lax security and high-handed behaviour during the crisis.
